history.origins: Rooted in the 19th-century Central European 'Jass' family. It arrived in Hungary via the Austro-Hungarian empire and was adapted to the 32-card Magyar KÃ¡rtya (Hungarian cards).
timeline: Late 1800s: Jass-style games spread in Hungarian coffee houses.
1920s: The name 'KlÃ¡ber' becomes the standard for the 4-player Hungarian variant.
1990s: Competitive KlÃ¡ber tournaments gain a revival in Budapest.
Present: A beloved traditional game, often played in families and social clubs.
history.cultural: The game uses the 'Tell' deck cards (Acorns, Leaves, Hearts, Gourds), adding a strong regional cultural flavor to the gameplay.
history.evolution: Transitioned from a two-player 'Jewish' Clob to a four-player partnership game, requiring much more defensive coordination between teammates.

setup.deck: 32-card Hungarian deck (ranks: 7, 8, 9, 10, AlsÃ³/Under, FelsÅ‘/Over, King, Ace).
setup.dealing: Cards are dealt counter-clockwise in batches (3-2-3 or 4-4). Each player receives 8 cards.
setup.equipment: 32-card Hungarian (Magyar Kártya) deck; scoring slate and chalk or equivalent.

rules.objective: Score more points than the opposing team through tricks and melds. The contractor team must outscore the defenders.
rules.gameplay: Must follow suit. If unable, MUST trump if possible. Trick-winning is counter-clockwise.
keyRules: Follow suit if possible; if unable, must trump if possible; otherwise play any card.
Player to dealer's right leads first; play is anticlockwise.
Bidding decides trump and contractor team; contractor must outscore defenders.
Melds (sequences, sets, bella) declared before first trick; only highest small meld counts per team, bella always scores.
Last trick worth 10 extra points; total card points 161. First to 501 wins the game.

strategy.basic: Partnership Communication: Only the highest meld declaration at the table counts for that point category. Communicate with your partner to ensure your team's best meld is prioritized.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Nine' Strategy: If your partner bids (takes), and you hold the Nine of trumps (Nell), try to lead it as early as possible if you suspect the opponent holds the Over-knave (Jass).
strategy.advanced: Defensive Ducking: If your team is the defender, don't always trump in. Sometimes it's better to lose a trick to save a high card for the 'Last Trick' (10 points).
tips: Always declare your melds before the first trick is played! Late declarations are usually void.
In the Gourds (TÃ¶k) suit, the cards can look similar; double-check your 'Over' and 'Under' knaves.

variations.name: Kontra / Rekontra / Szubkontra
variations.description: Before play, defenders may say kontra to double hand score; contractor may rekontra; defenders may szubkontra (8×). Does not apply on throw-in hands.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation only changes scoring multiplier; no engine constants overridden.

variations.name: Throw-in melds
variations.description: If any player holds a meld worth 100+ points (four of a kind or sequence of 5+), they must declare; hand is thrown in and meld points scored. Concealment penalized: opponents score 161.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Throw-in is a hand-ending condition; engine flow unchanged.

variations.name: Maccs (double game)
variations.description: If a team reaches 501 when opponents have less than 251, winners score a double game (maccs).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Double game affects match result only; no engine overrides needed.

scoring.description: Card points from tricks (161 total) plus last trick (10); melds (terc, kvart, sequences, four of a kind, bella) added. Contractor team must outscore defenders or defenders score all. First to 501 wins the game.
scoring.winCondition: Score more points than the opposing team in the hand; first team to reach 501 or more points wins the game.
